ShortDescription.Value: Fixes periodic service-coverage stutters without changing coverage results.

Publish.LongDescription:
Some cities experience a severe, rhythmic CPU stall while the simulation is running. At 1× speed, the hitch repeats approximately every 4.4 seconds and can freeze the game for 74–97 milliseconds. At higher simulation speeds, the same service-coverage workload runs more frequently.
**ETW tracing and native-code analysis identified the hotspot as:**
- Game.Simulation.ServiceCoverageSystem.ApplyCoverageJob.Execute()
This job combines the coverage paths generated by service providers such as parks, postal services, healthcare buildings, fire stations, and police stations.
The vanilla algorithm maintains an ordered list of active providers. Every time a provider advances to its next coverage element, the game reinserts its record into the correct position by shifting later records one position at a time.
In cities containing hundreds of service providers and extremely large coverage buffers, this can approach O(E × B) work, where E is the number of processed coverage elements and B is the number of active providers. The workload grows rapidly because adding more providers can increase both the number of elements being processed and the number of records that may need to be shifted for every element.
**Parks created the largest workload in the affected saves:**
- **Loon Lake:** 526 Park providers, approximately 1.11 million available coverage elements, and 507,000–512,000 processed per update. - **Providence Bay:** 523 Park providers, approximately 1.46 million available elements, and 457,000–478,000 processed per update. - **Dens-City, which did not exhibit the same rhythmic stutter:** approximately 49 Park providers.
That is why population and city size alone didn’t explain it in my testing. Dens-City can be enormous without triggering the same failure because it has roughly one-tenth as many Park coverage providers.
**This mod replaces the inefficient final merge inside ApplyCoverageJob with an exact, monotone radix queue.**
Instead of repeatedly moving provider records through one large ordered list, the replacement divides each 32-bit priority into four 8-bit sections. It uses those sections to place providers into priority buckets and tracks which buckets currently contain records. This allows the job to find the next provider directly without repeatedly shifting large portions of the list.
The replacement processes the same providers and coverage elements while preserving highest-coverage-first processing, equal-priority behaviour, the original floating-point calculations, serial write order, update frequency, budgets, and stopping conditions. It leaves the surrounding ServiceCoverageSystem stages unchanged, does not skip, approximate, delay, or reduce coverage updates, and does not add anything to the save file.
**Measured Result In the same Loon Lake test scene at 1× speed:**
**Without ServiceCoverageFix:**
- Average FPS: 43.8 - 1% low: 24.5 FPS - 0.1% low: 9.1 FPS
**With ServiceCoverageFix 0.3.2:**
- Average FPS: 52.8 - 1% low: 46.8 FPS - 0.1% low: 43.5 FPS
The largest improvement is in frame-time consistency. The severe periodic drop represented by the 9.1 FPS 0.1% low was eliminated during these tests. Results will depend on the city and hardware. Cities without unusually large service-coverage workloads may experience only a small improvement.
**Compatibility and Safety:** The replacement was validated against vanilla behaviour using 4,374 ordering cases, 1,038 randomized scheduler trials, finite floating-point edge cases, and stress tests containing up to 65,537 providers. On unverified game versions, the mod validates compatibility before enabling and otherwise leaves vanilla behaviour untouched. Removing the mod fully restores the original implementation. Intended as a temporary fix until the underlying issue is addressed.
**Current Limitations:** This diagnostic release targets one proven service-coverage performance failure. It does not claim to eliminate every source of stutter in Cities: Skylines II. A separate spike observed at 3× simulation speed can remain even after all Park coverage has been removed (that system being mail because it was the second heaviest workload in both of my cities), it's still under investigation and is not fixed by this release.
**Disclaimer:** I was going to keep this unlisted, but after a few people reached out facing a similar problem, I've decided to make it public. I've tested this mod for over 24 hours, saved, removed the mod, loaded the city again, simulated, reactivated the mod, loaded the city and simulated. I've done my best to make sure this is extremely stable and effective, but I have my own limitations. I really just wanted to be able to make videos on my cities again.
P.S. If you're curious about the computer-science idea behind why changing an algorithm can produce a huge performance increase, [this Veritasium video is a great intro](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kS-CGkiPetQ). It discusses Dijkstra and priority-based processing. This mod does not use Dijkstra, but it exploits a related property: its next coverage priority can only move in one direction, which lets it use a monotone radix queue instead of the game's repeatedly shifted sorted array (stutter producing method).

ChangeLog.Value: Validates the coverage bridge before installing the patch and checks exact coverage field layouts. Tracks live replacement execution, managed versus Burst execution, and vanilla fallbacks. Coverage calculations are unchanged.
